summary: Map urban food access, assess affordability and plan feasible city food actions. Explore the five-day intermediate course and enrol.
lede: Urban food security planning examines how city growth affects food availability, access, utilization and stability. It is for food security practitioners, municipal planners, market analysts and programme leads who need to turn local evidence into feasible actions. You’ll practise mapping neighbourhood access in QGIS, interpreting staple-basket affordability, assessing informal retail and supply dependencies, and prioritizing actions with indicators and responsibilities.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for people who already work with food access, urban services, food markets or local planning and need to connect that work to urban food security decisions. It is especially relevant when your role involves interpreting local evidence, coordinating municipal action or reporting programme priorities.
modules: FAO Urban Food Agenda and City Growth
Milan Pact and Informal Food Retail
FAO Urban Agriculture and Land Choices
New Urban Agenda and SDG Alignment
prerequisites: Working familiarity with food security, food markets or urban planning is expected. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with QGIS installed for the mapping exercise.
